title: Matched treatment-scenario matrix and semantic comparability contract
purpose: Define conservative, auditable comparison families across B0, B1, B2, and provisional T1 without treating shared columns, curated scenario counts, or protocol-specific timing as equivalent evidence.

classification_definitions.QUALIFIED_MATCH: At least two treatments share a high-level initial condition, fault or observation boundary, and outcome dimension, but protocol assumptions or execution semantics differ. Only the explicitly allowed fields may later be compared.
classification_definitions.DIAGNOSTIC_FAMILY_ONLY: Cases illuminate a related failure boundary but differ materially in attacker capability, activation timing, retry policy, initial alignment, or state-deletion behavior. They may be discussed side by side but must not be aggregated as matched treatment observations.
classification_definitions.TREATMENT_SPECIFIC: No defensible cross-treatment counterpart is currently defined.
classification_definitions.NON_OUTCOME_GUARD: A guard or rejection test that does not produce the common terminal outcome population and is excluded from treatment-effectiveness comparison.

alignment_class.rule: Map SYNC(<epoch>) to SYNC; preserve G_AHEAD, S_AHEAD, DIVERGED, and LOCKED as categorical classes.

metric_semantics.reason: The current baseline adapter uses one catalog case as one adapter contact and declared scenario-level transmission counts, while T1 uses explicit contact advancement, retries, and seeded or serialized schedules. Matching field names does not make those units equivalent.

comparison_families.name: Passive operational-key compromise followed by fresh recovery material
comparison_families.shared_condition: The currently active operational or traffic key is attacker-known, the long-term recovery root or authority remains available, and the attacker is passive during the recovery transition.

members.role: operational-key compromise with long-term update enabled
traffic-key exposure followed by fresh update

qualifiers: The treatments rely on different uncompromised roots and update assumptions.
A successful abstract outcome is not a cryptographic PCS proof.
Only categorical post-transition state may be compared after implementation validation.

comparison_families.name: No-fault state transition or recovery completion
comparison_families.shared_condition: No injected delivery, ordering, replay, restart, or evidence fault occurs during the modeled transition.
qualifiers: T1 begins from G_AHEAD while the listed baselines begin synchronized.
B1 includes two activation-policy variants and must not be double-counted as independent treatment observations.
This family compares terminal categories, not protocol cost or latency.

comparison_families.name: Delivery loss before safe shared activation or completion
comparison_families.shared_condition: A required pre-completion delivery is absent and the treatment reaches its modeled terminal or exhausted state.

members.role: ratchet update dropped after sender evolution

qualifiers: Initial alignment, compromise state, retry policy, and sender-state deletion differ materially.
B2 has already advanced and deleted prior sender state, unlike the other cases.
Use only as a structured qualitative boundary comparison.

comparison_families.name: Post-local or post-spacecraft activation confirmation evidence loss
comparison_families.shared_condition: One endpoint may have completed or activated while final confirmation or authenticated completion evidence is unavailable.

members.role: confirmation budget exhausted after spacecraft activation

qualifiers: B1 and T1 place activation and retained evidence at different protocol boundaries.
The B1 variants are alternative policies, not independent samples.
Outcome labels may differ because the models encode different evidence-retention semantics.

comparison_families.name: Post-convergence status telemetry loss
comparison_families.shared_condition: Both endpoints have converged on the new abstract key state, but expected status telemetry is absent.

members.role: status telemetry lost after both endpoints evolve

qualifiers: The status messages and verification procedures are abstract and treatment-specific.
The comparison is limited to convergence-versus-evidence separation.

comparison_families.name: Replay after successful state advancement
comparison_families.shared_condition: A stale or duplicate state-advancing control message is presented after the treatment has already reached its new state.
qualifiers: The replayed message types and replay-cache semantics differ.
Counts may be compared only after the D2 validator confirms one injected replay per member.

comparison_families.name: Ordering fault at a required exchange boundary
comparison_families.shared_condition: A message or fragment is observed outside the expected protocol order.

members.role: reordered response rejected before normal response succeeds

qualifiers: B1 aborts the exchange while T1 injects and rejects a malformed-order message before continuing.
The fault opportunities and retry behavior are not equivalent.

comparison_families.name: Persisted-state rollback or endpoint restart during transition
comparison_families.shared_condition: An endpoint loses or restores state in a way that invalidates the in-progress or recently advanced transition.

members.role: spacecraft pending state lost before commit

qualifiers: A stale persistent rollback and a volatile pending-state restart are not the same fault.
This family records a shared state-loss theme only.

scenario_disposition.reason: Master and traffic-key compromise has no matched B1, B2, or T1 scenario under the current abstractions.
Passive sender-state exposure has no current counterpart with the same attacker capability.
Receiver-state exposure and future-key traceability are specific to the B2 abstraction.
Both-endpoint state exposure has no matched current scenario.
Active sender-state impersonation assumes a treatment-specific attacker capability.
Spacecraft-ahead target negotiation has no current baseline counterpart.
Single prepare-loss retry is a T1 retry-policy test, not matched to no-retry baseline cases.
Single response-loss retry is a T1 retry-policy test.
Single commit-loss retry is a T1 retry-policy test.
Single confirmation-loss retry is a T1 retry-policy test.
Candidate command-isolation test does not enter the common terminal outcome population.
Unauthorized-authority rejection is a guard test.
Pending-capacity rejection is a guard test.
Conflicting-commit rejection is a guard test.

population_rules: Do not pool the 21 curated baseline catalog rows with the 12 seeded T1 pilot rows.
Do not treat multiple B1 policy variants in one family as independent replicates.
Do not calculate treatment success percentages from unequal, curated scenario catalogs.
Do not use a diagnostic-only family in quantitative cross-treatment aggregation.
Any future matched execution must instantiate the same family condition separately for each treatment and preserve treatment-specific exceptions.
Any field not explicitly allowed by a family is excluded from that family comparison.
remaining_blockers: Implement an executable matched-family population rather than relying only on catalog cross-references.
Define family-specific denominators before viewing comparative aggregates.
Validate equivalent fault opportunities and observation cutoffs for every quantitative family.
Freeze the statistical and descriptive analysis plan before publication-candidate execution.
Resolve or transparently retain the open external-review limitation.
